dynamical-spacetime.title: Einstein Field Equations with Cosmological Constant
dynamical-spacetime.description: Governs the gravitational dynamics of spacetime curvature in response to the distribution of mass-energy and momentum, establishing spacetime as a dynamical participant rather than a static background.

holographic-link.title: Ryu-Takayanagi Entanglement Entropy Formula
holographic-link.description: Relates the quantum entanglement entropy of a boundary subregion to the area of a minimal bulk surface in a holographic duality, bridging quantum information and spacetime geometry.

variational-foundation.title: Hamilton's Principle of Stationary Action
variational-foundation.description: Establishes that the physical trajectories of fields or particles are those that render the action functional stationary under all variations vanishing at the boundaries.

nuclear-cross-sections.title: Differential Nuclear Cross-Section
nuclear-cross-sections.description: Defines the differential nuclear cross-section as the ratio of the number of scattered particles per unit solid angle per unit time to the incident particle flux, governing the probability of specific scattering or reaction events.

quantum-tunneling-nuclear.title: Gamow Tunneling Probability and Coulomb Barrier Penetration
quantum-tunneling-nuclear.description: Formulates the quantum mechanical tunneling probability through the electrostatic Coulomb barrier for two interacting nuclei, governed by the Gamow parameter \eta.

pp-chain.title: Proton-Proton Chain Fusion Energy Generation Rate
pp-chain.description: Expresses the specific energy generation rate of the proton-proton chain fusion reactions as a non-linear function of stellar density, hydrogen mass fraction, and temperature.

parallax-baseline.title: Trigonometric Parallax Distance Relation
parallax-baseline.description: Formulates the trigonometric relation between the distance d of a celestial object, the parallax baseline b, and the observed parallax angle p, establishing the primary astronomical metric for local distance measurements.

parsec-definition.title: Trigonometric Parsec Definition
parsec-definition.description: Defines the parsec as the absolute physical distance at which an astronomical unit baseline subtends a parallax angle of exactly one arcsecond.

adiabatic-processes.title: Poisson Adiabatic Gas Relation
adiabatic-processes.description: Governs the pressure-density relation for a fluid parcel undergoing adiabatic expansion or compression without heat exchange, characterized by the adiabatic index \gamma.

topological-bh.title: Gauss-Bonnet Theorem for Horizon Topology
topological-bh.description: Relates the integrated Ricci curvature of a stationary black hole event horizon to its Euler characteristic, topologically constraining the horizon to a genus zero sphere.

unitarity-physics.title: Unitarity and Probability Conservation
unitarity-physics.description: Formulates the mathematical definition of a unitary operator, guaranteeing probability conservation and the preservation of inner products during quantum state evolution.

kappa-mechanism.title: Stellar Opacity Perturbation Relation
kappa-mechanism.description: Expresses the Rosseland mean opacity as a power law function of stellar density and temperature, governing the radiative transport perturbations that drive stellar pulsations.

interstellar-extinction.title: Cardelli-Clayton-Mathis Extinction Law
interstellar-extinction.description: Expresses the ratio of monochromatic extinction to total visual extinction as a function of inverse wavelength and the total-to-selective extinction ratio, characterizing interstellar dust grain properties.

hubble-telescope-astrometry.title: Hubble Centroid Astrametric Precision Limit
hubble-telescope-astrometry.description: Formulates the fundamental astrometric precision limit for centroiding a point source, scaling directly with the diffraction-limited angular resolution and inversely with the signal-to-noise ratio.

jwst-astrometry.title: Infrared Astrometric Centroid Precision
jwst-astrometry.description: Formulates the diffraction-limited astrometric centroiding precision in the infrared regime as a function of the observing wavelength, primary aperture diameter, and signal-to-noise ratio.

tov-equation.title: Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff Hydrostatic Equation
tov-equation.equation: \frac{dP}{dr} = -\frac{G M(r) \rho}{r^2} \left(1 + \frac{P}{\rho c^2}\right) \left(1 + \frac{4\pi r^3 P}{M(r) c^2}\right) \left(1 - \frac{2 G M(r)}{c^2 r}\right)^{-1}
tov-equation.description: Governs the relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium of a spherically symmetric compact object, correcting the Newtonian gravity equation with general relativistic pressure and curvature factors.

hr-diagram.title: Stellar Luminosity-Temperature-Radius Relation
hr-diagram.description: Relates a star's total electromagnetic luminosity to its physical radius and effective surface temperature, establishing the fundamental mathematical coordinate grid of the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram.

redshift-astronomy.title: Relativistic Doppler Redshift Relation
redshift-astronomy.description: Formulates the relativistic Doppler redshift for a source moving radially away from an observer, establishing the mathematical link between spectral shift and relative velocity.

flux-luminosity.title: Inverse-Square Law for Flux and Luminosity
flux-luminosity.description: Formulates the inverse-square relation between the observed energy flux and the absolute luminosity of a celestial source in an expanding universe, using the luminosity distance.

accelerated-expansion.title: Deceleration Parameter with Cosmological Constant
accelerated-expansion.description: Defines the dimensionless deceleration parameter in terms of the cosmic scale factor and its temporal derivatives, demonstrating that a dominant dark energy density leads to negative deceleration (acceleration).

galactic-rotation-curves.title: Centripetal Rotation Velocity Relation
galactic-rotation-curves.description: Relates the circular orbital velocity of a star or gas parcel to the enclosed mass within its orbit, serving as the primary mathematical evidence for the existence of dark matter halos.

mond.title: Modified Newtonian Acceleration Relation
mond.description: Modifies Newton's second law of motion in the low-acceleration regime, introducing an interpolation function and acceleration constant to account for flat galactic rotation curves without dark matter.

hot-dark-matter.title: Hot Dark Matter Free-Streaming Scale
hot-dark-matter.description: Formulates the free-streaming distance scale of hot dark matter particles, demonstrating how light, relativistic particles erase primordial density perturbations on sub-galactic scales.

mass-discrepancy.title: Dynamical-to-Baryonic Mass Ratio
mass-discrepancy.description: Expresses the dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratio as a function of the local baryonic gravitational field and the critical acceleration constant, characterizing the mass discrepancy in rotationally supported systems.

non-relativistic-degeneracy.title: Non-Relativistic Fermi Degeneracy Pressure
non-relativistic-degeneracy.description: Formulates the non-relativistic degeneracy pressure of a Fermi gas, demonstrating that the pressure scales with the five-thirds power of the number density and is independent of temperature.

relativistic-degeneracy.title: Relativistic Fermi Degeneracy Pressure
relativistic-degeneracy.description: Formulates the ultra-relativistic degeneracy pressure of a Fermi gas, showing that the pressure scales with the four-thirds power of the number density, leading to gravitational instability in massive compact objects.

quantum-resistance.title: Fermi Energy of Degenerate Electron Gas
quantum-resistance.description: Formulates the maximum kinetic energy occupied by electrons in a fully degenerate Fermi gas at absolute zero temperature, dictating the quantum resistance of dense stellar matter to gravitational compression.

stability-threshold.title: Chandrasekhar Mass Limit
stability-threshold.description: Formulates the maximum stable mass of a star supported by electron degeneracy pressure, beyond which no physical equation of state can resist gravitational collapse.

curvature-of-spacetime.title: Einstein Spacetime Curvature Relation
curvature-of-spacetime.equation:
G_{\mu

u} -  rac{1}{2} R g_{\mu

curvature-of-spacetime.description: Relates the Einstein curvature tensor representing the local geometry of spacetime to the stress-energy tensor representing the local mass-energy and momentum distribution.

poisson-equation-gr.title: Relativistic Generalization of the Poisson Equation
poisson-equation-gr.description: Formulates the Newtonian limit of general relativity, showing how the active gravitational mass density is corrected by pressure contributions in curved spacetime.

peculiar-velocities.title: Cosmological Peculiar Velocity Field
peculiar-velocities.equation: \mathbf{v}(\mathbf{k}, a) = i a f(a) H(a) \frac{\mathbf{k}}{k^2} \delta(\mathbf{k}, a)
peculiar-velocities.description: Relates the peculiar velocity field in Fourier space to the linear density perturbation field, showing how gravitational growth drives large-scale cosmic flows.

hubble-lemaitre-law.title: Hubble-Lemaître Law
hubble-lemaitre-law.description: Formulates the linear cosmological relation between the recessional velocity of a distant galaxy and its luminosity distance in an expanding homogeneous universe.

redshift-definition.title: Redshift Definition in Expanding Spacetime
redshift-definition.description: Defines the cosmological redshift as the ratio of observed to emitted wavelengths, proving that spectral expansion is physically tied to the scaling of the cosmic metric.

neutron-superfluidity.title: Quantized Superfluid Circulation in Neutron Cores
neutron-superfluidity.description: Formulates the quantum of circulation for neutron Cooper pairs inside a superfluid neutron star core, where the circulation of the velocity field is quantized in terms of Planck's reduced constant and the neutron mass.

spallation-physics.title: Cosmic Ray Spallation Production Rate
spallation-physics.description: Formulates the cosmic ray spallation production rate of a light isotopic species as the integral over energy of the product of the energy-dependent spallation cross-section and the incident cosmic ray flux.

quasi-static-equilibrium.title: Quasi-Static Stellar Energy Equation
quasi-static-equilibrium.description: Formulates the quasi-static energy conservation equation in a stellar interior, relating the spatial luminosity gradient to the nuclear energy generation rate and the temporal entropy change of the contracting gas.

kelvin-helmholtz-timescale.title: Kelvin-Helmholtz Timescale Relation
kelvin-helmholtz-timescale.description: Formulates the Kelvin-Helmholtz timescale for a self-gravitating sphere of gas, defining the thermal timescale on which a star radiates away its gravitational potential energy at a constant luminosity.

red-giant.title: Red Giant Branch Core-Mass Luminosity Relation
red-giant.description: Formulates the steep core-mass luminosity relation for shell-burning red giant stars, showing how the stellar luminosity is almost entirely determined by the mass of its degenerate core.

vogt-russell-theorem.title: Mathematical Representation of the Vogt-Russell Uniqueness Theorem
vogt-russell-theorem.equation: \left\{ R, L, T_{\text{eff}}, P(m), T(m) \right\} = \mathcal{F}\left[ M, \left\{ X_i(m) \right\} \right]
vogt-russell-theorem.description: Formulates the Vogt-Russell uniqueness theorem, showing that the global parameters and internal profiles of a star are uniquely determined by its total mass and the spatial distribution of its chemical composition.

mass.title: Stellar Mass-Luminosity Relation
mass.description: Formulates the fundamental mass-luminosity scaling relation for main-sequence stars, showing how stellar energy output is extremely sensitive to total gravitational mass.

chemical-composition.title: Fully Ionized Mean Molecular Weight Relation
chemical-composition.description: Formulates the mean molecular weight of a fully ionized stellar plasma as a function of its hydrogen, helium, and heavy element mass fractions.

mass-conservation-equation.title: Stellar Mass Conservation Equation
mass-conservation-equation.description: Formulates the fundamental first equation of stellar structure, relating the spatial gradient of the enclosed mass to the local density of the self-gravitating fluid.

energy-generation-equation.title: Stellar Energy Generation Equation
energy-generation-equation.description: Formulates the fundamental third equation of stellar structure for static stars, relating the spatial luminosity gradient to the local density and the nuclear energy generation rate.

convection.title: Schwarzschild Criterion for Convective Instability
convection.description: Formulates the Schwarzschild stability criterion, establishing that convective instability occurs when the radiative temperature gradient exceeds the adiabatic temperature gradient.

adiabatic-lapse-rate.title: Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate
adiabatic-lapse-rate.description: Formulates the spatial adiabatic temperature gradient (lapse rate) for a hydrostatic gas column, defining the rate at which temperature decreases with height under adiabatic expansion in a gravitational field.

stellar-boundary-conditions.title: Photospheric Stellar Boundary Condition
stellar-boundary-conditions.description: Expresses the boundary condition at the stellar surface (photospheric layer) under the Eddington approximation, relating the surface pressure to the surface gravity and Rosseland mean opacity.

standard-solar-model.title: Standard Solar Model Boron-8 Neutrino Flux Scaling
standard-solar-model.description: Formulates the power-law temperature dependency of boron-8 neutrino production in the stellar core, serving as a highly sensitive thermometer to validate the Standard Solar Model against terrestrial measurements.

mass-distribution.title: Spherically Symmetric Mass Distribution Integral
mass-distribution.description: Relates the cumulative enclosed mass within a radius r to the radial density distribution of a self-gravitating spherically symmetric body.
